question: Why are game-status columns blank for most Week-11 clubs?
answer: As of the Wednesday 2026-11-19 read only the Thursday-game clubs (IND HOU) printed Out/Questionable/Doubtful designations; CIN and WAS print explicit 'No Injuries Reported'; all other clubs' Game Status cells are empty. Blank is published as blank - never as zero. See F-TV-03.

question: Does a club with no rows on the injury report have no injuries?
answer: No. Two different states are kept separate: 'No Injuries Reported' (explicit page text = zero on report) versus a bye week (club not on the report at all because it does not play). Absence from the report is never treated as proof of health because no reserve/IR list was read. See F-TV-06.

question: How is net injury count defined?
answer: Count of players on the club's official report with a printed game-status designation (Out + Questionable + Doubtful) as of the read clock. It is blank - not zero - when designations are not yet printed for that club's game. Practice-status counts (DNP/LP/FP) are published separately and are always populated for clubs on the report.

question: Why are starters_out and replacement_named empty?
answer: No official announced-starter source and no official depth-order source were read in this session. The brief forbids inference, so both columns are blank for all 32 clubs and flagged (F-TV-01 F-TV-02). The gates are K-027 (starter evidence) and K-035 (depth source).

question: How is the W10 to W11 delta computed and when is it blank?
answer: Club-level difference of the same printed metric between the two reads (W10 final designations vs W11 Wednesday state). Delta cells are blank whenever either side is missing (bye) or unpublished (W11 designations not printed). Only IND HOU CIN WAS have a computable designation delta right now. Practice and listed-count deltas are computable for the 22 clubs that played both weeks. See F-TV-04.

answer: First-hand fetch_page reads of reg11 (255 rows incl. 2 explicit no-injury entries) and reg10 (347 rows) on 2026-11-19. question: What does 'delta not level' mean for this desk?
answer: The decision signal is the change between reads (delta), not the raw level. Levels are still published - with their read clocks - because the brief's per-team view asks for starters out replacements named and net injury count; but every level row carries its clock and every comparable pair carries a delta row. See S-02 for the automated series.

question: Are kickoff times ET?
answer: The schedule pages print times without a zone; the injury-report game headers print e.g. '8:15 PM EST'. November 22-23 2026 is after US daylight saving ends so Eastern = EST. kickoff_printed stores exactly what the schedule page showed; the EST reading comes from the injury-report headers (S-01).
